title: UNDERSTANDING STROKE: CAUSES, WARNING SIGNS AND PREVENTION
nextLesson: HOW DOES HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE DAMAGE THE HEART AND BLOOD VESSELS?

o: A condition affecting only the heart
An interruption of blood flow to part of the brain, or bleeding in the brain
questions.good: Correct! Stroke happens when blood flow to the brain is interrupted or a brain vessel ruptures.
questions.hint: Think about the organ that loses its normal blood supply.
questions.review: What happens inside the brain during a stroke?

o: A blockage in an artery supplying the brain
Too much oxygen entering the lungs
questions.good: Exactly! An ischaemic stroke occurs when a clot or another obstruction blocks blood flow to the brain.
questions.hint: Think about what happens when a blood clot blocks a vessel.
questions.review: Ischaemic stroke and blocked brain arteries.

o: The brain receives too much oxygen
A blood vessel ruptures and causes bleeding in or around the brain
questions.q: What happens during a haemorrhagic stroke?
questions.good: Correct! A haemorrhagic stroke involves bleeding from a ruptured blood vessel in or around the brain.
questions.hint: Remember the difference between a blocked vessel and a ruptured vessel.
questions.review: Haemorrhagic stroke and bleeding in the brain.

questions.q: Which condition is a major risk factor for stroke?
questions.good: Well done! High blood pressure is a major risk factor because it can damage blood vessels.
questions.hint: It is a condition that may have no obvious symptoms.
questions.review: High blood pressure and stroke risk.

questions.q: Which of these can increase stroke risk?
questions.good: Correct! Diabetes and high cholesterol can increase the risk of stroke.
questions.hint: Think about medical conditions that affect blood vessels and circulation.

questions.q: What does the F in F.A.S.T. stand for?
questions.good: Correct! F stands for Face. Look for sudden facial drooping or an uneven smile.
questions.hint: Ask the person to smile and observe both sides of the face.

o: Give the person food and water
questions.q: What should you do if someone suddenly develops possible stroke symptoms?
questions.good: Exactly! Suspected stroke requires immediate emergency medical attention.
questions.review: Emergency action when stroke is suspected.

o: A temporary interruption of blood flow causing stroke-like symptoms
A type of broken blood vessel in the leg
questions.q: What is a transient ischaemic attack, or TIA?
questions.good: Correct! A TIA causes temporary stroke-like symptoms and needs urgent medical assessment.
questions.hint: The symptoms may disappear, but the warning should not be ignored.
questions.review: TIA and the risk of a future stroke.

o: Exercising regularly and eating a balanced diet
questions.q: Which habit can help lower stroke risk?
questions.good: Excellent! Healthy eating and regular physical activity can help reduce stroke risk.
questions.hint: Think about habits that support healthy blood vessels.
questions.review: Lifestyle choices that help prevent stroke.

o: It helps healthcare professionals make urgent treatment decisions
To decide when the person should sleep
It is only needed for a routine appointment
questions.q: Why should someone note the time stroke symptoms began?
questions.good: Correct! The time symptoms began, or when the person was last known well, helps clinicians decide which treatments may be appropriate.
questions.hint: Think about why emergency doctors need to know how long symptoms have been present.
questions.review: Why timing matters in emergency stroke care.

disclaimer: This lesson is for educational purposes only. It does not replace medical advice, diagnosis or treatment from a qualified healthcare professional. If stroke is suspected, seek emergency medical help immediately.
